manifest.name: Rust Implicit Debt Analysis
manifest.description: Identifies hidden technical debt in Rust code comments by scanning for implicit work items outside of standard TODO or FIXME tags. This manifest tracks `file_extension`, `has_todo`, and `todo_summary` to enable agents to prioritize maintenance and refactoring efforts across 99 files.

analyzers.name: implicit-todo-finder::file-content::default
analyzers.description: Identifies implicit work items and technical debt in code comments, excluding standard tags like TODO or FIXME.

fields.name: has_todo
fields.description: True if implicit work items are found.

fields.name: todo_summary
fields.description: A concise summary of the implicit work items found in that file.

fields.name: file_extension
fields.description: The file extension without the leading dot (e.g., `js`, `md`), or `null` if none.

fields.F1: The module documentation describes the test suite as a 'stop-gap' measure to prevent local persistence writes, suggesting a temporary solution.
Identified a 'Temporary bandaid' comment regarding large MCP and image-generation payloads for remote clients, indicating a need for a more permanent solution.
Local fingerprints are computed for future attribution features, though not currently uploaded.
Comment on line 236 indicates that the `Custom` variant exists because protocol reshaping is non-trivial on the current branch, suggesting future architectural work.
The manual export process for this module is temporary and will change in the future.
Found implicit work items regarding future milestones (debounce/spinner), removed background events, and currently unused aliases.
Found implicit work items regarding legacy config compatibility and current directory handling inconsistencies.
Contains legacy OAuth compatibility logic for empty-scope requests and validates configuration overrides that are not currently applied.
The code defaults to lenient parsing for all models to avoid the complexity of threading a strictness parameter through call sites.
The LegacyManagedConfigTomlFromFile variant is kept as a 'best effort' because the original scheme did not work as intended; it needs to be phased out in favor of requirements.toml.
Uncertainty exists regarding whether the grant_root field in ApplyPatchApprovalParams is actually honored by the agent.
Multiple instances of deprecated `cwd` field usage suppressed by `#[allow(deprecated)]`, indicating pending migration. Test harness contains workarounds to simulate production runtime state.
Legacy shell tool is kept registered while unified exec is model-visible, indicating a potential future cleanup or deprecation task.
Consider changing the MCP connection manager initialization to use Option or OnceCell.
Identified implicit tasks to remove legacy filesystem policy projections and to stop expanding mutated arguments on the config object as it is being phased out.
Future compaction logic must preserve the guardian policy as exact top-level developer context.
Move hard-coded patch budget logic into model capabilities if it changes often.

Found 3 implicit items: 1) Legacy support for 'ghost_snapshot' settings is retained despite the feature being removed. 2) Warning logic for inline bearer tokens should be removed after a few months. 3) A suggestion exists to refactor deprecated field auditing to check individual config layers instead of the merged result.
The 'awaiter' role configuration is commented out with a note stating it is 'temp removed', indicating a pending decision on its status.
The code mirrors the server-side retained-message default, implying a need to update or align this logic once the server-side path changes.
Currently only supports first-party clients; future support for other clients is implied.

The code warns that the cookie store is process-global. If future callers need user-specific cookies, the store must be refactored to be scoped to the auth/session owner. Additionally, the Cloudflare cookie allowlist must be kept aligned with documentation.
Pending implementation for input-rewrite, permission-rewrite, and short-circuiting capabilities in PermissionRequestDecisionWire; fields currently fail closed.
Contains feature flags marked as temporary, prototypes, or legacy no-ops indicating technical debt and future cleanup requirements.
Future implementation of a remote backend for the storage interface.

Consider allowing the no-arg case for head if individual shell command components are verified in the future.
The test `test_ls_dash_al` currently fails and is expected to pass only after the `option_bundling` feature is implemented.
The comment 'Naive matching implementation' suggests the current argument matching logic is intentionally simple and may require optimization or a more robust algorithm in the future.

The comment 'For now, we parse only commands like `122,202p`.' indicates that the current implementation is limited and temporary, implying a need to support additional sed command formats in the future.
The file contains a comment indicating the code is kept for future wiring but is currently unused.
